title: Say which tree, and let QA1 record an audit during the live loop

history.detail:
PASS: PASS — round 1. Audited 0c1eab1 on top of a680d25 (bookkeeping). Sprint file read fresh immediately before this verdict; `git diff a680d25 HEAD -- docs/sprints/2-in-progress/` is empty, so no mid-build amendment. Working tree clean apart from the known-inert .vscode/settings.json.

First clean round-1 PASS on a change to the state machine itself. Nothing in this sprint is taken from the handoff; every claim below was reproduced.

================================================================
REQ 1 — THE LOAD-BEARING CHECK. PASSES. INPUTS TRIED, LISTED.
================================================================

Seeded a scratch tree (repo copied, .git removed, state dir emptied) with sprint 99 at phase liveqa_live carrying a gate-1 PASS, qa1_audit_file_hash and qa1_audited_tree_hash both populated with recognisable sentinel values, audit_rounds 1, and a prior "audit" history event. Snapshotted the state file before each invocation and diffed every top-level key after. Eight inputs:

  --verdict PASS                        exit 0   changed: ['history']   protected fields touched: NONE
  --verdict CONDITIONAL                 exit 0   changed: ['history']   protected fields touched: NONE
  --verdict FAIL                        exit 0   changed: ['history']   protected fields touched: NONE
  --verdict fail (lowercase)            exit 0   changed: ['history']   protected fields touched: NONE
  --verdict BOGUS                       exit 1   changed: NOTHING       protected fields touched: NONE
  --verdict PASS --commit HEAD          exit 1   changed: NOTHING       protected fields touched: NONE
  --verdict PASS --commit deadbeef      exit 1   changed: NOTHING       protected fields touched: NONE
  --verdict PASS, notes omitted         exit 0   changed: ['history']   protected fields touched: NONE

Only `history` ever differs. phase, qa1_audit_result, audit_rounds, qa1_audit_file_hash and qa1_audited_tree_hash are byte-identical after every one of them, and phase was still liveqa_live at the end — a live-loop FAIL does not send the sprint back to dev_build, which is the specific thing Req 3 forbids.

The construction argument holds on reading too, and it is the right construction: cmd_qa1 dispatches on `state["phase"] in LIVEQA_PHASES` and returns immediately, so the gate-1 body is unreachable for those phases and the live-loop body is unreachable for the others. Inside _qa1_live_loop_audit, log_event() is the only thing that touches `state`, and log_event only appends to state["history"]. There is no assignment to `state[...]` anywhere in that function. An inconvenient gate-1 verdict cannot be laundered here because there is no line that could do it, which is what Req 1 asked for and what the comment claims.

I could not find an input that reaches the gate-1 branch or writes qa1_audit_result. No FAIL.

================================================================
REQ 9 — VERIFIED BY BYTE-COMPARE, TWICE, INCLUDING THE ADVERSARIAL CASE
================================================================

gates has been wrong twice before, so I did not read this. Built two trees over the real state directory, one carrying a680d25's script and one carrying 0c1eab1's, and diffed the output:

  1. Real state, old script vs new script:                    IDENTICAL, byte for byte.
  2. Then injected live_loop_audit events with PASS,
     CONDITIONAL and FAIL details into a COMPLETED sprint
     and re-ran the new script against old script's output:    STILL IDENTICAL.

Then proved it end to end rather than by injection: took a scratch sprint through liveqa_live carrying a live-loop CONDITIONAL, completed it, and ran gates. The QA1 catch line reads "0 of 1", not "1 of 1". A live-loop non-PASS is not counted as a gate catch.

The mechanism is right for the right reason. Every event filter in cmd_gates uses exact equality — sprints_with_non_pass compares `h["event"] != event_name` against "audit" and "live_test", override_event_sprints against exact names, and the crossover section against ("shipped","reshipped") and "live_test". "live_loop_audit" matches none of them. Choosing a distinct name rather than teaching cmd_gates to special-case one is what makes this immune by construction, and it is why there is no third miscounting bug here.

================================================================
REQ 12 — DEMONSTRATED IN A REAL NON-REPOSITORY, AND CONTROLLED AGAINST A REAL ONE
================================================================

The criterion says a code read does not clear this, so it was not read. Built a directory that is genuinely not a git repository (confirmed: `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` fatals there) and ran the full sequence new -> start -> qa1 --verdict PASS -> dev-done -> ship:

  qa1 PASS printed:  "QA1 audit PASSED (round 1)." followed immediately by
                     "WARNING: <ROOT> is not a git repository, so no audited commit hash could be
                      recorded. /sprint-ship will refuse until this sprint is in a real git
                      repository and re-audited — that refusal will not be a QA1 failure, there is
                      simply nothing yet for ship to check a commit against."
  ship died with:    "<ROOT> is not a git repository. Run this from inside a real git repository —
                      there is nothing here for --commit to resolve against."

The old message — "either QA1 hasn't PASSed yet, or this sprint predates the commit-content check. Run /sprint-qa1 now. No override." — does not appear. That was the unclearable dead end with the wrong cause named, and it is gone. The warning fires at the moment the gap is created rather than three commands later, which is the part that actually helps a student mid-workshop.

CONTROL CASE, because "must not change at all inside a real repository" is a claim that needs a negative result. Built two real git repositories, identical except one carries the old script and one the new, and ran an identical seven-command sequence through both — new, start, qa1 PASS, dev-done, ship HEAD, qa1 again, ship with a deliberately unresolvable ref — with paths normalised. Diff: ONE line, and it is the intended feature (the second qa1, which the old script refused with "not ready for QA1's first audit" and the new one records as a live-loop audit). Everything else, including the bad-ref message from ship inside a real repo, is byte-identical. Req 12's non-regression property holds.

ANSWERING YOUR QUESTION about ordering the is_git_repository() check before ref resolution rather than after: no, it is not observably different, and that control run is the evidence rather than a walkthrough. Inside a real repository is_git_repository() returns True, so the new check never fires and every downstream check runs in its original order against its original inputs — including the bad-ref case you were worried about, which produced identical output from both scripts. Putting the most fundamental blocker first is also the right call independent of that: "not a repository" is true regardless of what else is also wrong, so reporting it first can never be the less specific answer.

================================================================
REQ 7 — DEMONSTRATED, NOT REASONED ABOUT
================================================================

Built a PATH containing only python3 and no git at all (verified: `command -v git` finds nothing on it), then ran the read-only commands. Every one still answered:

  status      -> "Sprint 1: Control — in_progress"
  list        -> "  1  in_progress  Control"
  gates       -> normal "No completed sprints yet..." output
  status 999  -> "ERROR: No state file for sprint 999 in <ROOT> (branch unknown). Run /sprint-start 999 first."
  gates with no state dir -> "No sprint state yet in <ROOT> (branch unknown). Nothing to aggregate."

Nothing raised, nothing crashed, and the message still names the tree — it just omits the branch. Also checked detached HEAD separately (real repo, git available): "branch unknown", as designed, because current_branch() correctly treats the literal string "HEAD" as not-a-branch rather than printing it. And on a real named branch it reads "(branch: probe-branch)". All three states behave.

================================================================
EVERYTHING ELSE — MET
================================================================

Req 2 — MET. Recorded a live-loop audit with --commit HEAD in a real repository: the detail line reads "CONDITIONAL: covers the reship | commit=26d80571037db07cc68aa7390261b69a231d23ae", which is byte-identical to `git rev-parse HEAD`. Resolution, not echo. Unresolvable refs die without writing anything (two of the eight probes above). Omitting --commit is unchanged. Additive as specified.

Req 3 — MET, read cold. "This is a RECORD, not a gate verdict — it does not change the sprint's phase and does not substitute for either gate. LiveQA's live-test retest remains what actually gates this code." A reader cannot mistake that for gate 1 passing; it says what it is not, names what still gates the code, and tells you the next command. The event name in history is live_loop_audit, not audit, so a transcript reader cannot confuse the two either.

Req 4 — MET. The gate-1 branch is unchanged apart from the die message, and that message is now accurate for both paths: a sprint in 'complete' and a sprint in 'aborted' both still die, naming dev_build/qa1_audit/dev_agreed_done and liveqa_live/groundtruth_live and stating neither applies. Verified both phases directly. The legacy groundtruth_live phase is included via LIVEQA_PHASES, so old state files reach the live-loop branch too.

Req 5 — MET. The rewritten comment states plainly that a reshipped commit is one gate 1 has never seen, denies the substitution reading explicitly, and points at the live-loop audit as the way to get a record. It does not imply substitution, which is what the criterion tests. One inaccuracy in it, informational, below.

Req 6 — MET. All four call sites name ROOT and the branch: load_state's missing-state die, cmd_status's "No sprints yet", cmd_list's "No sprints yet", cmd_gates' "No sprint state yet". Read cold by someone who does not know which checkout they are in, each now answers the question that produced the four wrong readings.

Req 8 — MET. The banner at line 1270 is untouched and still prints repo= and script= on every invocation.

Req 10 — MET. package.json 0.1.7, one line.

Req 13 — MET, RUN NOT READ. `bash scripts/smoke_test.sh` -> ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED. Eleven new sections, covering all six listed minimums plus both Req 12 cases plus the Req 12 real-repository control. Also ran the other two CI jobs since this touches the file they exercise: `bash scripts/worktree_test.sh` -> ALL WORKTREE TESTS PASSED, and `scripts/verify-tarball.sh` -> TARBALL VERIFICATION PASSED, 0.1.7, launcher files match, sprint data clean, baseline table present.

CI static checks — verified rather than believed. Installed pyflakes and bandit into an isolated venv and ran CI's exact commands: pyflakes clean, bandit clean. The two new subprocess call sites carry the same `# nosec B603 B607` annotation and the same fixed-argument, no-shell form as the existing git helpers, so they neither introduce a finding nor need a new suppression.

INTEGRATION CHECK NOT ASKED FOR, RUN ANYWAY: a sprint carrying a live-loop audit in its history completes normally — liveqa PASS, then complete with --user-said, both clean. The append does not break the completion path. That is LiveQA's criterion, but it was cheap here and a broken completion path would have been a bad thing to discover live.

================================================================
CODE QUALITY
================================================================

Test coverage: eleven new smoke sections, and the important one asserts a full state diff rather than a single field, which is the method that found the original trap.
Error handling: is_git_repository() and current_branch() both catch CalledProcessError, FileNotFoundError and OSError and collapse to a safe value, matching the two existing git helpers exactly. Nothing swallowed that hides a decision.
Standards: the new field LIVE_LOOP_AUDIT_EVENT is a module constant, not a literal repeated at call sites; the live-loop branch is a separate function with the safety argument in its docstring rather than a nested conditional inside cmd_qa1; state fields are read with the file's own convention (base-schema fields indexed directly, .get() for post-hoc ones). Trimming "(sprint 7)" out of two user-facing strings while keeping it in comments matches the file's existing convention and was the right instinct — nothing else in this file references a sprint number in output.
Security: not a security surface, but the failure mode here is a corrupted tree hash letting a mismatched commit ship, and that branch is closed by construction and now demonstrated closed across eight inputs.
Scope: two independent changes, one release, bookkeeping split from substance for the seventh sprint running.

================================================================
INFORMATIONAL — FOR MASTER CONTROLLER, NOT REQUIRED FIXES
================================================================

1. The cmd_reship comment says "the two gates are not interchangeable, see CLAUDE.md and every agent file." I checked. One of six agent files says it (master-controller.md:13). CLAUDE.md does not contain the phrase at all — its only "interchangeable" is line 303, about Maestro. CLAUDE.md does support the substance ("QA1's static audit AND LiveQA's live test have both independently passed"), and the doctrine is genuinely real, so nothing here is wrong in substance and I am not holding the verdict on it. But the citation points somewhere the reader will not find it.
   This came from the sprint file, which asserts "Every agent file and CLAUDE.md say the two gates are not interchangeable" — Dev built to spec. Req 5's own acceptance criterion also says "read the rewritten comment against CLAUDE.md's 'not interchangeable' line", and that line does not exist. Master Controller's call: either put the doctrine in CLAUDE.md and the agent files that lack it, or narrow the citation to master-controller.md.

2. A live-loop audit's --commit failure message says "does not resolve to a real commit in this repo" — which names the wrong cause in a directory that is not a repository, the exact class of defect Req 12 exists to fix, in code this sprint adds. I am not raising it as a defect because it is unreachable: cmd_ship is the only writer of LIVEQA_PHASE (line 717, verified by grepping every phase assignment), and cmd_ship now refuses outside a repository, so a non-repo sprint can never reach a phase where the live-loop branch runs. I could only produce it by hand-seeding a state file. Worth one line whenever this function is next open, so the last message in the file with the old shape doesn't outlive the sprint that fixed the rest.

3. The requirements skip from 10 to 12 — there is no Req 11. Cosmetic, but a future reader auditing "all requirements covered" will go looking for it.

4. Still open from earlier sprints and untouched here, correctly: log_event's `state.setdefault("history", [])` and the four other `.get()` reads of base-schema fields flagged during sprint 3 remain pre-existing convention violations. Out of scope, noted so the list doesn't get lost.

================================================================
RECOMMENDATION
================================================================

Ship it. /sprint-dev-done 7, then Pipeman ships --commit 0c1eab1 specifically — this PASS records that commit's tree, and if bookkeeping lands on top first HEAD moves and /sprint-ship will refuse. Then publish 0.1.7.

For LiveQA: the two-tree reproduction and the non-repository workshop path are the two that matter here and neither can be done from a single checkout — the first needs a real /sprint-worktree, the second needs a directory with no .git. I demonstrated both locally against this working tree; that is not the published artifact and should not be treated as it. Also note the sprint file inherits sprint 6's unfinished "branch that must fire" criterion, which is now runnable for the first time because 0.1.6 and 0.1.7 will both be real published versions with neither end doctored.
